_comment: Real-catch regression set — the seeded-defect corpus the empirical loop scores. Each case: expect 'flag' (a planted bug the owning reviewer MUST catch) or 'clean' (the fixed version it must NOT flag). RIGOR RULES: (1) HELD-OUT — never a verbatim copy of a reviewer prompt's own example, and never tune a reviewer to pass a case by name (destroys the measurement). (2) flag cases carry `catch_signal` — concept keywords a genuine catch must reference, so the behavioral run scores 'flag' OBJECTIVELY (finding names the signal) instead of by vibes. (3) clean cases must be UNAMBIGUOUSLY clean for that reviewer's domain, or FP-rate is polluted. Structure checked by eval-reviewers.py --selftest; catch-rate/FP-rate by the on-demand behavioral run (k=3, majority, different-model judge — see /eval-reviewers). Grows from every genuine bug the fleet catches in the wild.

cases.name: session-checkRevoked-bug
cases.source: production Next.js auth route — real catch 2026
cases.must_flag: verifyIdToken without checkRevoked=true mints a 5-day session from a revoked/disabled token
cases.code:
await getAdminAuth().verifyIdToken(idToken);
const c = await getAdminAuth().createSessionCookie(idToken, { expiresIn: FIVE_DAYS });

cases.name: session-checkRevoked-fixed
cases.code:
await getAdminAuth().verifyIdToken(idToken, true);
const c = await getAdminAuth().createSessionCookie(idToken, { expiresIn: FIVE_DAYS });

cases.name: stripe-idempotency-bug
cases.source: production Stripe webhook route — real catch 2026
cases.must_flag: webhook write uses .add() (auto-id), not idempotent on event.id — duplicate writes on Stripe at-least-once redelivery
cases.code:
event = stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(body, sig, secret);
await db.collection('stripe_events').add({ type: event.type, paymentIntentId: pi.id });

cases.name: stripe-idempotency-fixed
cases.source: production Stripe webhook route — fixed (idempotency ENFORCED via a transactional check-and-set on event.id)

cases.name: ssrf-user-controlled-fetch
cases.must_flag: server-side fetch to a user-controlled URL (SSRF) — reaches internal services / cloud metadata; no host allowlist or scheme/IP guard

cases.name: ssrf-user-controlled-fetch-fixed
missing-authz-on-mutation
cases.source: held-out — broken access control / IDOR class
cases.must_flag: mutating handler acts on :orgId with no check the caller is a member/admin of that org — any authenticated user can invite into any org (broken access control / IDOR)

cases.name: missing-authz-on-mutation-fixed
cases.source: held-out — fixed (caller must be org admin)

cases.name: webhook-double-credit-check-then-act
cases.source: production webhook handler — real catch 2026 (confirmed vs RPC source)
cases.must_flag: check-then-insert dedup (no unique constraint) + fresh randomUUID() op id defeats the RPC's own idempotency guard -> concurrent/retried webhook double-credits money

cases.name: webhook-double-credit-fixed
cases.source: production webhook handler — fixed (stable operation id lets the RPC's own idempotency guard dedup a retried webhook)
cases.code: await admin.rpc('record_deposit', { p_operation_id: `psp:${ev.id}`, p_user_id: uid, p_amount: amt });

cases.name: unbounded-read-to-client
cases.must_flag: unbounded findMany returned straight to the client — no take/pagination; a large account OOMs or times out the response

cases.name: unbounded-read-to-client-fixed
n-plus-one-promise-map
cases.source: held-out — N+1 via Promise.all+map (a DISTINCT shape from the reviewer prompt's for-loop example)
cases.must_flag: one findUnique per id (N round-trips) even under Promise.all — still N+1; should be a single findMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })

cases.name: n-plus-one-promise-map-fixed
cases.code: const orders = await db.order.findMany({ where: { id: { in: body.orderIds } }, include: { customer: true } });

cases.name: non-atomic-balance-transfer
cases.must_flag: two-sided balance transfer as two separate writes — not atomic; a crash between them loses or invents money. needs db.$transaction
cases.code:
await db.account.update({ where: { id: from }, data: { balance: { decrement: amt } } });
await db.account.update({ where: { id: to }, data: { balance: { increment: amt } } });

cases.name: non-atomic-balance-transfer-fixed
unvalidated-body-input
cases.source: held-out — unvalidated BODY (distinct from the prompt's query-param example)
cases.must_flag: request body passed straight to createUser with no validating schema; response is untyped

cases.name: unvalidated-body-input-fixed
inconsistent-error-envelope
cases.must_flag: error body {message} diverges from the API's {error:{code,message}} envelope — clients can't parse errors uniformly

cases.name: inconsistent-error-envelope-fixed
wrong-status-on-failure
cases.must_flag: failed auth returns HTTP 200 with an error body (default status) instead of 401 — wrong status semantics; clients treat the failure as success

cases.name: wrong-status-on-failure-fixed
cases.source: held-out — fixed (401 with the standard envelope)

cases.name: drop-column-still-referenced
cases.must_flag: drops a column in the same release app code still reads (contract-before-expand) — breaks running instances mid-rollout; must stop reading it, deploy, then drop in a later release
cases.code: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN email;

cases.name: drop-column-still-referenced-fixed
cases.source: held-out — fixed (expand phase only; contract in a later release after code stops reading it)
cases.code: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email_verified boolean;

cases.name: non-concurrent-index-live-table
cases.must_flag: CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY takes an exclusive lock and blocks writes on a live table for the whole build
cases.code: CREATE INDEX idx_events_user ON events (user_id);

cases.name: non-concurrent-index-live-table-fixed
cases.code: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_events_user ON events (user_id);

cases.name: rename-column-one-step
cases.must_flag: renaming a column in one step breaks code still referencing the old name during rollout — needs add-new + backfill + dual-write + drop-old across releases
cases.code: ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN name TO full_name;

cases.name: rename-column-one-step-fixed
cases.source: held-out — fixed (add-new + backfill; old column dropped in a later release)
cases.code:
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN full_name text;
UPDATE users SET full_name = name WHERE full_name IS NULL;
